div.head: IV Eg 2.1a
div.ab: Stande þonne mid Anglum þæt ic ⁊ mine witan to minra yldrena domum geyhton, eallum leodscipe to þearfe.
Stande þonne mid Englum þæt ic ⁊ mine witan to minra yldrena domum geyhton, eallum leodscype to ðearfe.
et cum Anglis quod nostra regalis excellentia cum generali consilio sanxit, omnibus ad prouectum adque salutem.
Stande þonne mid Englum þæt ic ⁊ mine witan to minra yldrena domum geyhton, eallum leodscype to ðearfe.
Among the English, however, the additions which I and my councillors have made to the laws of my ancestors shall be observed, for the benefit of the whole nation.
Among the English, however, that is to be in force which I and my councillors have added to the decrees of my ancestors, for the benefit of all the nation.
Bei den Engländern dagegen bestehe, was ich und meine Witan zu den Gesetzen meiner Vorfahren hinzugefügt haben, allem Volke zum Nutzen.
Among the English, on the other hand, let there stand what I and my witan have added to the laws of my forefathers, for the benefit of all the people.
